name: Regional Bloodlines of Clan Gangrel (Wolves at the Door)

text.content:
Source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book One: Animals

A strange, rarely-seen branch of Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} lurks in the dark corners and sewers of the great cities — Constantinople and Rome above all — rather than the wilderness the rest of the clan favors. Theories about their existence abound: that they are Crusaders trapped in the cities they meant only to pass through, the result of a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} experiment, or even members of an entirely new clan. In truth, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} have hidden in the cities of men since the first stone was laid in Babylon. Over the centuries, these Greek Gangrel (as they call themselves) have adapted to survival in an urban environment rather than a wild one: they have developed Obfuscate in place of the clan's usual Fortitude, and keep good relations with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} who share their sewers. Very few in number, most Greek Gangrel have appeared only recently in Constantinople, with at least one known in Paris. They have yet to attend a Gather, though some are said to want to build ties to the wider clan.

Source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book One: Animals

In the waters of the Black Sea, the Mediterranean and the Baltic lives a unique branch of Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel}: the Mariners. Where the typical @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} develops the traits of a land animal, the Mariners instead show signs of their watery homes — gills, scales, fins and puckered, fish-like mouths are common features among them. These Gangrel spend their unlives at sea, preying on sailors or feeding on fish, and avoid contact with other vampires, including their landbound kin. The only vampires with whom they have any regular contact are the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, and that contact is rarely friendly. Because of their unusual existence, the Mariner Gangrel have developed alternate applications of Protean unknown to the rest of the clan.

Source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book One: Animals

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} who followed the Moors into Iberia have developed their own distinct culture. Named after the small Muslim successor kingdoms of Iberia (the Taifas), these @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} see themselves as scholar-warriors fighting a religious war, and identify more closely with Islam and its Cainites than with the rest of Clan Gangrel. In practice, this means the Taifa Embrace only devout warriors; each new convert is paired with an elder Taifa Gangrel for both schooling and protection, and the pair spends its nights traveling Iberia to hunt Christian Cainites of every stripe. Occasionally a pair will work alongside an @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite}, though never for long. The Taifa have replaced the Gather with a semi-annual conclave at which no rites of status occur — those present simply defer to the oldest Gangrel in attendance — and many Taifa abstain from feeding on Muslims, preferring the vitae of Christians or Jews instead.
